title: G-ring
statement: Let $k$ be a field. A Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] $k$-algebra $A$ is *geometrically regular over $k$* if for every finite purely inseparable field extension $k'/k$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension] the ring $k'\otimes_kA$ is regular, i.e. Noetherian with every localization at a prime ideal a regular local ring [def-weil-regular-scheme] (Stacks Algebra, Definition 0382, by condition (2) of Lemma 0381, as recalled in More on Algebra, Section 07BY). A ring map $\varphi:R\to\Lambda$ of commutative rings is *regular* if it is flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] and for every prime ideal $\mathfrak p\subset R$ the fibre ring $\Lambda\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] is Noetherian and geometrically regular over the residue field $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ (More on Algebra, Definition 07BZ). A commutative ring $R$ is a *G-ring* if $R$ is Noetherian and for every prime ideal $\mathfrak p\subset R$ the ring map $R_{\mathfrak p}\to(R_{\mathfrak p})^\wedge$ is regular, where $R_{\mathfrak p}$ is the localization of $R$ at $\mathfrak p$, a local ring with maximal ideal $\mathfrak pR_{\mathfrak p}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], and $(R_{\mathfrak p})^\wedge=\varprojlim_nR_{\mathfrak p}/\mathfrak p^nR_{\mathfrak p}$ is its $\mathfrak pR_{\mathfrak p}$-adic completion with its canonical ring map $R_{\mathfrak p}\to(R_{\mathfrak p})^\wedge$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion] (More on Algebra, Definition 07GH).

standard facts on G-rings stated there (created by the split of lem-weil-pbc-finite-etale-lifting-limit-descent): Z, fields, Noetherian complete local rings (Proposition 07PS) and Dedekind domains of characteristic 0 are G-rings, and rings essentially of finite type over a G-ring are G-rings (Proposition 07PV; ubiquity Proposition 07PX); a localization of a G-ring is a G-ring (proof of 07PV)

the henselization of a pair (A,I) with A a G-ring is a G-ring (Stacks More on Algebra Lemma 0AH3, Greco Thm 5.3 i)), stated there (created by the split of lem-weil-pbc-finite-etale-lifting-limit-descent)

split_report.summary: Read More on Algebra Section 07BY with Definition 07BZ (regular ring map), Section 07GG with Definition 07GH (G-ring), Algebra Lemma 0381 / Definition 0382 (geometrically regular), 00OD/00KU (regular ring, regular local ring), 00HB (flat), 00CO and Section 07BH (localization at a prime, residue field), Fields 09HE (purely inseparable). Rewrote the statement to be self-contained: geometrically regular algebra over a field (Stacks 0382, taken in the form (2) of 0381, finite purely inseparable k'/k, as More on Algebra 07BY recalls it; the equivalence with (1) is a pointer, not part of the node), regular ring map (flat, fibre rings Noetherian and geometrically regular), G-ring (Noetherian, R_p -> pR_p-adic completion regular for every prime). Removed the claim 'equivalently every local ring has geometrically regular formal fibres' from the statement (Stacks' remark after 07GH; it is the definition of formal fibre unfolded and nobody uses it). No well-definedness theorem is needed: every clause is a predicate on objects given by the cited definitions (regular ring includes Noetherian; the completion and its map are def-weil-pbc-adic-completion; the fibre ring is Noetherian by requirement of 07BZ). stmt_deps: def-weil-regular-scheme (reviewed leaf IsRegularLocalRing/IsRegularRing), def-weil-pbc-adic-completion (reviewed leaf) and four new Mathlib leaves (Noetherian ring; flat module/ring map; localization at a prime, residue field, fibre ring; finite purely inseparable extension). Mathlib has no G-ring, regular ring map, geometrically regular algebra, formal fibre or excellent ring (three kinds of search recorded); it has IsRegularLocalRing, IsRegularRing, RingHom.Flat, Module.Flat, Algebra.FormallySmooth (discrete), Algebra.IsGeometricallyReduced, Ideal.Fiber, AdicCompletion. The source repository (both branches) has no G-ring/excellent/geometrically regular declaration; the only mention is the docstring of WeilConjectures/SixFunctors/Etale/Derived/Stability.lean:107 ('quasi-excellent Noetherian by Gabber').
